text:
ana: quick thread 0m run on a lightweight priming sensitivity pass for herald13b-int5 (new candidate). goal: measure how priming length & token-formatting affect quality drop vs int6.

colm: why int5? brief rationale?

ana: int5 seems to hit a latency sweet spot (~65ms p50 vs fp16 88ms) and cost middle ground (~$45/1M). hoping it keeps most fidelity of int6 with lower cost.

tera: numbers?

ana: summary: fp16 baseline p50=88ms cost $120/1M. int6 p50=70ms cost ~$52/1M. int5 p50=65ms cost ~$45/1M. int4 p50=58ms cost ~$38/1M.

ben: quality deltas on our slices?

ana: short: int5 weighted ROUGE-L ~ -0.9 vs fp16 (int6 -0.6, int4 -1.8). priming-sensitive slices (system prompts + few-shot examples) show larger degradation: int5 -2.2 RL, int6 -1.4, int4 -3.5. numeric EM losses track similarly.

colm: interesting. So priming is where int5 loses ground more. any hypothesis?

ana: looks like per-layer activation scaling interacts with prompt tokens that contain atypical punctuation (bulleted examples, code fences). attention quantization seems to amplify format-sensitive misinterpretation.

tera: ops/product question: what's the routing policy proposal?

ana: propose 3-tier hybrid: default -> int5 for typical chat (saves ~62% vs fp16), fallback -> int6 when: (1) prompt includes >1 code fence OR contains explicit few-shot examples (heuristic: lines with ">example" or "Input:"), (2) tokenized prompt length > 280 and contains structured markers ("---", "\n\nExample:"), OR (3) user is enterprise/hf opt-in. int4 reserved for lowest-latency dev tier.

ben: can we detect few-shot cheaply? regex + line-count should work. code fences cost nothing to detect.

infra-bot: rollout items:
- add config flag quant.herald.default=int5
- add predicates: code_fence_count, fewshot_indicator, token_count_structured
- metric: priming_fallback_rate per route + priming_failure_complaints
- canary: 3% traffic for 72h, shadow int6 for 4% traffic 24h
- alert if fallback_rate > 6% sustained or complaints spike

colm: what's expected avg unit cost with the fallback thresholds?

ana: estimate: default int5 $45, fallback to int6 7% traffic => weighted ~ $47.5/1M. fallback to fp16 negligible at <0.5% => +$0.3. so ~ $47.8/1M.

tera: scorecard snapshot (mock):
```
slice: short-chat            | FP16 RL 44.7 | INT6 RL 44.1 | INT5 RL 43.8 | INT4 RL 43.0 | cost ratio int5 0.38
slice: fewshot-priming       | FP16 RL 49.2 | INT6 RL 47.8 | INT5 RL 47.0 | INT4 RL 45.7 | cost ratio int5 0.38
slice: numeric-reasoning     | FP16 EM 80.1 | INT6 EM 78.9 | INT5 EM 77.4 | INT4 EM 74.2 |
human_accept: FP16 96.5% | INT6 95.6% | INT5 94.4% | INT4 92.1%
unit_cost_per_1M: FP16 $120 | INT6 $52 | INT5 $45 | INT4 $38
```

colm: ML ask: can you run a small per-layer int5 vs int6 attention-ff sweep focused on priming tokens? also include formatting-robustness test (fenced vs inline examples). how long?

ana: 36h sweep should do it (2xA100-80GB). will include 500 priming variants and measure token-format sensitivity & KL-based confidence signals.

ben: ops: please log per-request predicate hits and correlate fallback hits with complaint tickets. infra-bot: set dashboard tile "priming RL" and "priming_fallback_rate".

infra-bot: dashboard tiles created and reminder set for canary review in 72h.

tera: GTN messaging: "Herald13b-int5 offers a latency/cost middle ground for chat workloads; we automatically detect prompt formats that need higher fidelity and route them to int6 to preserve few-shot and code-fenced behavior." short blurb draft: @ana please iterate.

ana: will draft blurb. next steps: (1) implement predicates & canary (ops) (2) run per-layer & formatting sweep (ML) (3) 500-case priming-focused human eval + weekly scorecard (product owns) (4) GTN blurb draft.

colm: agreed. set tickets and owners. thanks team.

infra-bot: reminder scheduled for fallback_rate check in 72h and sweep completion in 96h.
